subject: Skylark - plan to rebalance GPUs from surge to steady-state
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@skylark.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Skylark - plan to rebalance GPUs from surge to steady-state

Elena —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion you saw a multi-week surge in inference volume driven by a new feature roll-out in July, and you’re now interested in converting some of that temporary burst capacity into a smaller but more predictable dedicated pool for Q4.

To get aligned I requested the last two months of token-level usage (attached) and sketched a simple rebalance approach: carve a steady dedicated tranche sized to 70% of 95th percentile sustained utilization, and keep a small burst pool for transient spikes. Before I formalize the pricing and tranche sizes I need two quick confirmations from you:

- Is there an internal SLO you want us to size for (p95 latency target / request SLA)?
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency / private deployment) that would require Dedicated vs Private?

If you’re good, I’ll circulate a proposed tranche matrix and a conversion addendum (no change to model versioning). Happy to do a brief call with Vanessa and Ben if it helps.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@skylark.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skylark - plan to rebalance GPUs from surge to steady-state

Rishi —

Thanks, attaching the usage export we pulled from our internal telemetry (same file you sent back but with labels). Our product SLO is 95th latency <= 400ms; we’re fine with Redwood keeping burst capacity in the same region (us-west) for now. No immediate residency change, still US only.

A couple notes:
- The July spike was a mix of more traffic and longer sequences from the new summarization mode.
- We expect a smaller bump around mid-September when we onboard a partner, but it should be short-lived (3–4 days).

If you can size a steady tranche that keeps us under our SLO and shows cost delta vs current burst-heavy setup, we’ll review and route to procurement.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, Skylark AI
elena@skylark.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skylark - plan to rebalance GPUs from surge to steady-state

Rishi / Vanessa —

Pulled the attached rough matrix overnight. My quick read: if we target the 70% of 95th percentile steady tranche Rishi suggested, Skylark moves from ~120 vGPUs of burst usage to ~48 dedicated vGPUs steady, with a 12-vGPU burst reserve for peak days. That gives ~28% cost savings VS purely burst billing assuming they convert to a 12-month reserved tranche.

Risks / ops notes:
- We need to verify sequence-length distribution in the CSV (Elena mentioned longer sequences). If avg seq > 1.5x baseline, effective throughput drops and tranche size should increase.
- We should propose an autoscaling policy that gracefully adds burst capacity when queue length > threshold instead of immediate overprovisioning.

I’ve attached a simple excel (proposed_rebalance_matrix.xlsx) with scenario columns (baseline / surge / partner-onboard). Want me to run a slightly different quantized kernel profile to check cost delta?

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

Ben / Rishi —

I agree with the numbers but want to flag procurement timing. Skylark’s procurement contact (cc’d only on external threads) typically requests a 30-day window for legal and invoice setup. If we recommend a 12-month reserved tranche we should include a transitional pricing line item for month 1 to cover any overage backfill while commit is established.

Suggested next steps (short):
1) Finalize tranche sizes and the conversion addendum (Ben to finalize numbers).
2) Send a 30-day transitional pricing addendum + standard SLA language (I can draft).
3) Set up a 45-minute call with Skylark procurement and ML Ops week of Sep 6 (Rishi to schedule).

I’ll draft the transitional wording and attach it to the DocuSign packet.

—Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations

Subject: Re: Skylark - plan to rebalance GPUs from surge to steady-state

Elena —

Thanks for the clarity and for confirming the SLO. Per the internal review above we propose the following:

- Dedicated steady tranche: 48 vGPU-equivalent units (region: us-west).
- Burst reserve: 12 vGPU-equivalent units (automatically available; billed only when used).
- Transitional month: prorated dedicated pricing + overage backfill protection for day 1–30 while procurement completes.
- SLA: p95 latency <= 400ms; we’ll include automatic fallback to a compatible model variant during sustained overload.

I’ve attached the rebalance matrix and will send a short addendum for review (DocSend link below). If you’re good, let’s schedule the procurement call next week — Sept 8 or 9 work for us.
